q2_gaps: Spatial PATH / route PP ('walks **along** the ridge'; likewise 'across', 'through', 'around', 'up'): the oblique inventory covers position (Location, exemplified 'in/at/on'), origin (Source, 'whence'), and destination (Goal, 'whither'), and routes a PP to the preposition-named oblique only when it names what the activity is 'about or directed at' (non-spatial) — a spatial path is none of these, so nothing determines whether it is (Location e ridge) or (Along e ridge), and two faithful parses can differ.
notes: Location is a defensible reading of the instruction set's 'does the PP answer where?' test and loses only the path shape, so I score it faithful; the underlying indeterminacy is reported as the coverage gap above.
